speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that; given your history of AIDS and these specific visual symptoms, I need to ask a few targeted questions to narrow down the cause. Have you noticed any floaters, flashes of light, or a sudden "curtain" over your vision in the right eye? Also, is your right eye currently red, painful, or associated with any new visual distortions?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis. Given your history of AIDS, recent fungal esophagitis, and Kaposi's sarcoma, along with painless floaters and decreased vision, CMV retinitis is the most likely diagnosis. I will request an urgent fundoscopic exam and CMV PCR to confirm this.
